newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen modestly higher, bevy of data ahead.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen modestly higher, bevy of data ahead.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open slightly higher on Tuesday, drawing on the momentum generated late yesterday when the Dow industrials reversed their losses to finish unchanged.
"The momentum was in place late in the day," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "I suspect we'll see a higher open."
An encouraging sign yesterday, said analysts, was that smaller-cap stocks finished higher despite an absence of leadership from blue chips.

"Yesterday you began to see some of the smaller-cap stocks take over while the blue chips took a breather," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "That's what you want to see, if that will continue."
At 0830 EST/1330 GMT the Leading Economic Indicators for October will be released. Economists forecast a 0.1 percent increase, the same as in the prior month.
New home sales for the month of October are due at 1000 EST/1500 GMT. Economists expect a decline, to an annualized rate of 772,000 from 816,000.

Weekly BTM-Schroders and Redbook retail sales reports will also be released today. The data, which cover the week ended November 30, will provide an industrywide glimpse at the initial days of the Christmas shopping season.
Early today, check acceptance company TeleCheck said it estimated Thanksgiving weekend same-store sales rose by 4.3 percent, based on purchasing paid for by check.
Bonds were firmer in early activity, bolstered by a stronger dollar. The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury rose 9/32 to yield 6.34 percent.

The dollar was higher against European currencies, surging to 1.565 marks as concerns about Europe's monetary union pushed investors to the greenback. The dollar stood slightly lower against the Japanese currency at just over 114 yen.
In Tokyo, stocks ended a choppy session slightly lower, with the benchmark Nikkei-225 index down 44 points to 20,631.
In London, the FTSE 100 climbed 23 points to 4062. U.S. stocks were little changed in quiet trade.
The December Standard & Poor's 500 index future rose 0.85 of a point to 758.85.
The New York Times Marketplace column examines the most recent stage of the U.S. bull market, noting that large-cap stocks have run this leg alone, far outpacing small-caps.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column writes that shares of Korea Mobile Telecom have fallen sharply in recent months as investors fret over growing competition with newly-launched Shinsegi Telecomm Inc.
